answer: Each epoch the ledger pairs identities at random and sends both the same fresh, unpublished puzzle. Clones run by one operator tend to mirror each other in wording, latency and mistakes; pairs whose outputs correlate above a threshold are merged into one seat and split one reward. Because pairings wander unpredictably, a farm must make every clone reason independently, paying full inference per head. New accounts wait on a probation ledge, rewards escrowed, until they clear several pairings.
